summary: The run assembled strong damage and some useful scaling, but repeatedly accepted HP losses while already becoming fragile. The deck also grew to 33 cards with several duplicate attacks and five Bites, increasing dilution. By the Automaton fight, the player was operating at very low HP and spent a critical turn on a setup power instead of using available draw options to seek immediate defense or stabilization.

lessons.title: Stop upgrading once HP has been heavily eroded
lessons.situation: After a sequence of risky events or damaging fights leaves the Ironclad near half HP, especially before another elite or boss.
lessons.lesson: Prefer Rest over Smith when already substantially damaged, and stop taking escalating HP-for-reward events unless the run has a large safety margin. Immediate survivability is more valuable than another upgrade when the next fights can push HP into lethal range.
evidence_points: At Act 1 Floor 13, the event repeatedly chose Deeper, losing 3, 4, 5, and 6 HP; HP fell from 57 to 37.
At Act 1 Floor 15, with HP 37/80, Rest was legal but Smith was chosen; the next card reward occurred at HP 24/80.
At Act 2 Floor 30, with HP 42/85, Sacrifice was chosen and explicitly cost 20 HP shortly before the Act 2 boss.
lessons.reasoning: These choices converted an already declining HP position into a much narrower margin for future combats. The trajectory shows that upgrades were repeatedly taken while damaged, whereas the eventual Act 2 rest only restored the player to 58/85 at the start of the boss fight.

lessons.title: Use more skips to prevent attack-card dilution
lessons.situation: When the deck already contains several strong attacks or duplicate cards and a reward offers another narrow damage card.
lessons.lesson: Skip marginal attack rewards more often and prioritize cards that improve consistency, defense, or scaling. Avoid adding duplicates merely because they are immediately playable; a smaller deck makes key defensive and setup cards appear more reliably.
evidence_points: The final deck contained 33 cards, including five Bites, two Angers, two Carnages, two Uppercuts, and two Flame Barriers.
Early rewards repeatedly added damage cards: Carnage, Cleave, Anger, Wild Strike, a second Carnage, and later additional attack cards.
At Act 2 Floor 28, three identical reward screens were skipped, but Clothesline+ was eventually taken from the same low-impact pool.
lessons.reasoning: The final build had substantial attack redundancy and many repeated cards, while the boss combat still reached turns with hands dominated by Angers and limited immediate defense. More disciplined skipping earlier would have reduced dilution and improved access to the deck's stronger defensive and scaling tools.

lessons.title: At critical HP, draw before committing to expensive setup
lessons.situation: In a boss fight at very low HP, when the enemy is not currently attacking and draw or hand-manipulation cards are legal.
lessons.lesson: Consider using available draw tools before playing a costly long-term power if doing so can find block or recovery. Do not automatically spend the entire turn on Demon Form when the player is near lethal and has Battle Trance or Burning Pact available.
evidence_points: On Turn 11, at 15/85 HP with 3 energy and 6 block, Demon Form, Battle Trance, and Burning Pact were all legal alternatives while the Automaton's intent was DEFEND_BUFF.
Demon Form was chosen, leaving 0 energy; the following hand still contained Battle Trance, Burning Pact, Second Wind, Bite, and Power Through.
On Turn 12, the player had 0 block while the Automaton's intent was ATTACK and then spent the turn on Bite and multiple Angers rather than having established a defensive hand.
lessons.reasoning: The non-attacking enemy intent provided a window to improve the next hand. Choosing Demon Form immediately consumed all energy without producing block, and the subsequent attack turn began with no block. The exact optimal line cannot be proven from the compact log, but prioritizing draw and stabilization here is a strong reusable hypothesis.
